title: Distributed representations of behaviour-derived object dimensions in the human visual system
goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Predict each original participant’s single-trial fMRI voxel responses to THINGS images from the source image-wise 66-dimensional behavioural embedding. Retain the related Figure 6 category-versus-dimension attribution as a separate source analysis, not a substitute primary score.
primary_outputs: Candidate method and outputs for the source task: Predict each original participant’s single-trial fMRI voxel responses to THINGS images from the source image-wise 66-dimensional behavioural embedding. Retain the related Figure 6 category-versus-dimension attribution as a separate source analysis, not a substitute primary score.

Source-paper comparison for Original per-voxel 12-session cross-validated Pearson r; published Figure 2 map-to-primary aggregation unresolved: Primary source code returns per-voxel Pearson r between predicted and observed responses, averaged across the 12 folds. Figure 2 visualizes noise-ceiling-corrected R2. Exact conversion and masks for a published-comparable scalar remain unresolved; signed SSE/SST R2 cannot silently replace correlation-squared.
success_criteria: Recover and pin the complete original three-participant input/mask/row/session manifest and numerical author outputs for Figure 2.
Fix the original fold-wise Pearson metric, any noise-ceiling conversion and aggregation before candidate development; compare the candidate to the original 66-dimension author encoding result.
Preserve all original participants, sessions and eligible voxels; a family/category holdout, changed population or narrowed voxel subset is a separately labelled extension.
Freeze candidate, access/resource budgets, task-specific meaningful effect and valid paired uncertainty before final scoring.
Do not count reproducing Figure 6 variance partitions, lower reconstruction error, or stronger p values as a Figure 2 prediction win.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.
